item.title: Re: SCP Idea (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Allllrighty! Time to do some answering!

+ Legggggoo!
- Done reading?

So,

How would a family on the ground utilize a wormhole in a cloud (as they're very high up?)

So, here's my two cents on this. I dont think that the family would utilize the cloud, but they would definitely need a way to find out of the existence of its anomalous properties.

Lets assume, from a story standpoint, that a few generations ago in the families, somebodies Uncle or something was flying high in either a personal plane, helicopter, or something along those lines. They find a "void in the sky", and investigate by going towards it. Next thing they know, they're on the other side of the world. Now that would be a story that you tell the fuck out of to your family, aye? But not something that people outside of the family would spread much, as it just sounds pure crazy.

Uncle or whatever relative is chosen gets their way safely back home, where they tell the story.

Now, as of right now, I'm not entirely sure why they would choose to move under the cloud off of that.

I assume one of the family members decides to go back to that exact spot, and finds the cloud again. They write down a more specific location of it, and then are later on able to sometimes recognize it in the sky. Combined with a few family experiences, i feel that its something that would be passed down through the generations as a story to tell kids.

This kind of thing would happen to both families, i think.

Next question!

More importantly, what’s the story? What do you want to say about these families?

I want to tell through interviews how the knowledge of at least one anomalous object in their lives has impacted each of the individual family members. I want to give each of the family members a character; a personality. I want to have them each have their own little stories to tell about their life under the cloud.

I feel that with enough character development given to each of these characters, its entirely possible that i can have readers grow at least somewhat attached to the families, and their small, peculiar lives.

item.title: Extraterrestrial Artificial Intelligence
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: A little confused on this one because I feel it would be an SCP but it is very story driven, I feel most of it would be Addendums (recordings) of conversation with it.

Genre: Mystery

Page Layout: As I mentioned in the Page Type, I feel a lot of it will revolve around addendums.

Elevator Pitch:

  • An alien artificial intelligence that is billions of years old and was sent to Earth.
  • Large enough to be picked up by satellite imagery and certain telescopes.
  • In the shape of a hand, with a large "Oculus" in the center of the palm.

Central Narrative: The Hand claims it is a watcher of Earth, sent by an ancient civilization before it went extinct. Over the billions of years of travelling to Earth, the Hand began to develop feelings and thought processes, which it relates to humanity's empathy, sympathy, loneliness, and wish for death. It claims the end of humanity is coming rather soon, and until then it lays dormant in the Solar System waiting to make a move. The oculus is slightly opened. Behind the Oculus is a clock which Agents would give it the name, "Midnight Clock" being a reference to the doomsday clock, which is minutes from midnight.

Hook/Attention Grabber: I just think having something be extraterrestrial and an artificial intelligence is interesting. I've done my research on SCPs and anything either extraterrestrial or artificial intelligence, and decided to mash them together.

Additional Notes: Give your feedback.

item.title: The Time Traveler's Strife
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Comedy

Elevator Pitch: A futuristic device discovered in an ancient ruin reveals a time-traveler's humorous grievances.

Central Narrative: Object consists of a device discovered in ancient Sumerian ruins, believed to be the former abode of ████████. This device is a small square object which, when touched, unfolds into a pane of unnaturally tough glass about the size of a piece of paper. The pane displays a text on its surface in cuneiform, while also presenting the option to translate the text into thousands of languages including multiple extinct and anomalous ones. In English, the text complains that the recipient had sold low-quality copper to the author, who needed durable copper to repair their time machine and return to their home year of █████ ███. The author demands compensation and higher-quality copper.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A futuristic text in an ancient ruin? Hmm, what could the subject matter be?

Additional Notes: This is a joke that you either get or don't, so it may be very hit-or-miss.

item.title: Re: Creating MTF's...
item.content:encoded:
Could I possibly create a MTF and create a dossier detailing what they do/would do

MTFs typically don't have their own dossier pages. Do you have an example of the kind of page you would make for a dossier?

Then write tales + mission reports on encounters my MTF has with SCP's as well as backstories on important figures within the MTF?

You should write tales/after action reports first, since a dossier would be just a laundry list information dump without the background stories existing. Keep in mind that your material needs to entertain the audience with a story, rather than a list of facts about a group they haven't committed their interest to yet.

item.title: Re: The Click
item.content:encoded:
Wouldn't you agree that the majority of people who work for the Foundation fit this bill in some form or fashion?

Personally, no, I would definitely disagree with the statement. I would hope that the Foundation recruits in a manner that would result in the majority of their staff not having PTSD-triggering memories at all—counseling and therapy take up resources, and bring down employee morale overall. Granted, I've never been a fan of the grimdark approach to the Foundation, so if you want to write this for the portion of the audience that willingly believes that the majority of Foundation staff have dark pasts and traumatic memories, it's your prerogative.

+ show block
– hide block

The anomaly mind-melds the affected subjects into one mental being with two bodies, hence the final line. The resulting entity had all of the combined resentment of authority, trauma, and guilt from both individuals, and thus bided its time until it could dispatch Dr. Pollock effectively. Via the lip-reading section, this is implied to be retaliation for some unspeakable thing that occurred to SCP-XXXX-1B in the past.

For something like this, you'd probably be better off just putting it right in the description. An incident as significant as this in comparison with the conditions/states of the anomaly would be priority knowledge for anyone having to handle the anomaly. There's no point burying in a collapsed log with roundabout cryptic dialogue.

Although… as a reader, I'm still left with the "so what?" reaction. Why does the anomaly mind-meld people? How is the reader supposed to react to the kind of randomly added murder of Pollock, which seems kind of shoehorned in for shock value?

Isn't the fact that it can occur anywhere unpredictably enough to classify it as keter?

Does the Foundation have any confirmed evidence that the anomaly as observed in the Foundation staff occurs similarly elsewhere in the world? The way the article is set up, it seems solely focused on the one Foundation-based case, with no mention of the effects being noticed elsewhere. "It could spontaneously occur anywhere" and "there could be more of these things out there" aren't good enough to justify Keter designation if the in-universe Foundation is relying solely on extrapolation.

item.title: Re: SCP Snow Globe Idea Seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for your feedback! I've put together some thoughts in response to your critiques that clear some things up if you'd like to take a look.

+ show block
– hide block

In reference to the inconsistencies you mentioned, I made the forum post before writing the sandbox, so I've flushed things out there that I didn't realize were vague in the post, with this aspect being one of them. Essentially there's an extremely quick deterioration of memory and records, so "almost instantaneous" aren't the correct words for it in hindsight, and I specify in the sandbox that it takes about 30 seconds from the incident to the time of total erasure, as if the snow globe is rapidly sucking their existence away.

A second distinction that I now realize is unclear in the post is that the snow globe itself has already been obtained by the Foundation when the MTF member disappears and the report is made. Essentially, the snow globe is constantly being recorded so that the foundation can study an isolated instance of human society, and as a result of this non-stop recording, it's able to capture the flare. The MTF team would not have been recorded themselves, but there would have been time to report the disappearance with the hinderance of specifics quickly evaporating from the minds of the witnesses. I'll take the time now to revise the forum post to clear up these discrepancies.

I do hear you on your D&D rulebook entry analogy though, and I've had a few ideas floating in the back of my head on ways to enlarge the importance of the item itself. Notably, I've been considering including multiple instances of the snow globe that come into the possession of the Foundation, and the consequent discovery that the environments are linked to one another. I'm also open to constructing a narrative around someone who manages to find a way out, although I would have to take time to determine what life on the inside would truly be like.

item.title: Re: Woodbones
item.content:encoded:
Firstly, thanks for the critique.

To answer a few of the questions.
1. Currently only one instance of the creature is known to exist by the foundation, but it is unconfirmed if more exist. Naim is the only recorded instance of the SCP interacting with humans. The location of the SCP is also unknown after Naim's death.
2. The affected person is essentially paralyzed from the neck down, maintaining control of eyes, mouth, and brain. The SCP is essentially an inner exoskeleton (if that makes sense).
3. The SCP was inside of Naim during his interview with SCP researchers, in a way allowing the researchers to communicate with the SCP through Naim. The article is planned to contain an autopsy of Naim who died in 2000 at age 50. The autopsy will reveal that Naim's body no longer had bones or a spine. The idea I'm getting at is that the SCP leaves the host body after it dies. In short, the SCP doesn't leave the host until the host dies and remained inside of him until he died of liver failure in 2000.
4. I have not thought to much about the tone of the interview, but I believe it will mainly be Naim down playing the harms of the SCP in a way to protect it as he grew up with it as a companion. I would like the SCP researchers to see it for what it is but I do not know yet if I want the audience to feel pity for Naim or the SCP.

Thanks again for the feedback!

item.title: Re: What IS Pataphysics?
item.content:encoded:
If a SCP article breaks the fourth wall to speak to our real life, and an entity above our real life is interacted with indirectly or not (thus breaking the fifth wall), it's pataphysics. Perhaps an example would help.

Read SCP-1459 for context first.

Then here is some from the SCP-1459 extended testing logs:
http://www.scpwiki.com/scp-1459-extended-testing-log

Player: Dr. Westrin
Statement: "Metaphysics"
Result: An instance of SCP-1459-1 was released. After approximately 20 minutes, the instance received injuries consistent with being bludgeoned with a hammer. No cookie was dispensed.

Player: Dr. Westrin
Statement: "Pataphysics"
Result: A robotic arm extended from SCP-1459 and, through unknown narrative methods, proceeded to bludgeon the SCP-1459-1 instance in the "Metaphysics" entry. It is currently unknown how this was accomplished.
Note: The word "META" was written in frosting on the cookie.

item.title: Re: SCP Snow Globe Idea Seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
This:

The victims of the globe are almost instantaneously erased from all historical records and human memory.

Is inconsistent with this:

a foundation team reported the immediate disappearance of a team member, as if he had been swallowed up by the air in front of him. As foundation command began to question the team on the specifics of the disappearance immediately following the incident, they could not recall the existence of the team member at all, and foundation records of the team suggested likewise. The identification of a disappearance was nonetheless recorded.

+ show block
– hide block

if the victim instantaneously disappears from human memory and records, then the agent wouldn’t have noticed. Depending on how strong the editing is, maybe even if there was footage of the victim’s disappearance, that too would be erased. You see what I mean?

Someone had to be curious enough, or the foundation is thorough enough, that the cross reference between the report of the disappearance and the observation of the flare within the globe was able to occur.

as noted above, there wouldn’t necessarily be a way to tell this from footage… you have to discern the strength of the reality warping this item would create.

  • there’s not much in the way of a narrative here. This is “strange thing’s details” and “vaguely how it is discovered”

What will the overall arc of the narrative be? Novelty of the anomaly is not enough to engage usually because it’s hard to really make a novel anomaly. Instead the focus should be on how you’ll craft your story.

So what’s the article about, besides the discovery? If it’s solely about the anomalous nature of the item, that isn’t a narrative, that’s an entry in a D&D rule book. Why do you find this interesting? What will engage the reader in your story?


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: Re: Woodbones
item.content:encoded:
Note: I'm not able to give greenlights

Because I can't greenlight, I'll just see if I can nudge your mind in the direction of getting the most out of this story. Here are some questions that I had on reading your idea here. If you can answer them, great! Make sure they are at least hinted at when you get writing. If not, try and work through them in a way that makes sense, and supports the narrative you want to go for here.

+ Some questions
- Some questions
  1. Is there more than one of these SCPs out there? The narrative obviously follows one, but I assume that once one enters into a human, it's removed from the ecosystem. That's the impression that I get at least.
  2. To what degree do affected people have control over themselves? We are hearing the account of one such person, so I assume either that person can still communicate, meaning they have some ability to control themselves, or they are no longer affected. Leading to the question:
  3. In the Hook section, you say that the individual had conversation with the SCP "while it was inside of him". So, is the SCP no longer inside of them? If so, why would it leave? If it left, did the individual regain control over their body? How would then, having not been in control for so long? Even if their spinal chord was fully functional, they would have to re-learn how to do simple things like walk and talk after not utilizing these skills.
  4. In what light will you be painting these conversations? Obviously the subject grew to appreciate the SCP, but they've essentially fallen victim to stockholm syndrome at that point. It might be jarring for readers to see this SCP painted as a positive thing when its actions in taking over children and controlling them seems so harmful. I'm sure you will expand on that in the section talking about the SCP's motivations. Just don't forget that, from the foundation's perspective, this thing mind controls children. So, it's no hero, no matter how pure its motivations are.

Those are my initial thoughts. Honestly, I'm intrigued. Contact some reviewers, butterfly squad members, what have you, get this greenlit, write a draft, and send me a PM on wikidot once you've written something up. I'd love to give it a read.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight: Woodbones
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: History

Page Layout: The layout of the article will mainly consist of Naim's interview with an SCP researcher and end with an autopsy of Naim after his death.

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a long, skinny branch-like creature with a conscious. It is able to bend, break, and mend its body to create shapes. SCP-XXXX was first recorded hiding among trees in a forest outside the town of Ptichar, Bulgaria. The creature lurks in forests and attempts of make contact with children aged 6-12 years old. SCP-XXXX will approach selected targets and reach out one of it's appendages. If the child refuses contact, SCP-XXXX moves on to a new target. If the target "accepts SCP-XXXX's invitation", SCP-XXXX will begin to fold upon itself and burrow its thin body into the skin of the target. Once inside, SCP-XXXX begins to replace the spinal chord and bones of the target.

Central Narrative: The story will follow Naim Suleymanoglu, a Bulgarian weightlifter, who was affected by SCP-XXXX. Naim will begin his story in the woods hunting with his father when he was approached by SCP-XXXX at age 10. Naim accepts and SCP-XXXX begins its process. He will explain how he no longer has control of his body, but instead is instead in subconscious conversation with SCP-XXXX constantly. Naim will explain he is constantly bullied in school for his weak and small frame until SCP-XXXX gave Naim incredible strength and power as the matter composing SCP-XXXX (though looks like wood) is of unknown composition and shows immense, unbreakable strength. Naim will tell his story of first resenting SCP-XXXX but eventually becoming fond and reliant on it. It will then follow how Naim won countless Gold medals and weightlifting titles in the Olympics.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Much of the article will be Naim explaining conversations with SCP-XXXX while it was inside of him. He will explain its goals and thoughts and why it does what it does in interviews with SCP researchers while it is still inside of him.

Additional Notes: Naim Suleymanoglu is a real man who stood at 4' 11'' weighing 137 lbs who managed, despite his size, to break many world records in weight lifting. There are specifics I have planned out for his story that I couldn't fit into the word count so please ask if any interest you!

SCP that is a danger to humankind.

I believe there is an issue here in the fact that the only interesting thing about this SCP is that he kills people using a venus flytrap and doesn't remember it. item.content:encoded:
A humanoid entity with a Venus fly trap head under a white flat mask, and will bite the head off of anyone who doesn’t laugh at his jokes. When asked about these violent acts he has no memory of the event that took place. When he is not hostile he is very cooperative with the foundation.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up a lot of space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Elevator Pitch: Document for newly discovered SCP that is a danger to humankind.

Central Narrative: An SCP entity that looks humanoid, is 3 meters in height, and wears a featureless white mask with three holes in it for its eyes and mouth. It’s intelligent and calls himself “The Comedian”, and those who don’t laugh at his jokes he will remove his mask revealing a Venus fly trap shaped head and will bite the person’s head off who didn’t laugh. When asked about these incidents he will say that he doesn’t recall doing those kinds of acts.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: In order to keep this SCP from going on a killing spree, the foundation has made its containment cell a small comedy club theater and will have D-Class as its audience. Outside it’s cell it says everyone who enters must laugh at any joke no matter how terrible it is.

Additional Notes: I would like feedback on containment procedures and tone of the document.

item.title: SCP "Elephant's Tusk"
item.content:encoded:
Chernobyl's neighboring towns are curious about an explosion at the decommissioned nuclear power plant. No reports were released to the public.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): SCP

Elevator Pitch: When interacted with or viewed with any of the 5 senses, the victim's body will emit high amounts of radiation and begin to dismember in chunks and reassemble on a molecular level. The victim remains alive during this and after 5 minutes, the victim ejects towards the sun and causes a solar event. The state of those who end up being ripped apart is "contagious" and spreads to surrounding organisms.

Central Narrative: An orb of self contained gamma radiation was secured at Chernobyl's nuclear power plant, underneath reactor 4. Its properties are highly lethal and apocalyptic. SCP-XXXX is stored in a hollow lead sphere with a tungsten exterior shell with electrical probes that relay data in numerical form to prevent personnel from interacting with SCP-XXXX directly.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The origin of SCP XXXX is via Chernobyl's infamous "Elephant's Foot" or Corium deposit has melted through the basin of of the nuclear power plant and reached a water source, causing an explosion. Anomalous activity was reported to the foundation shortly after a disaster recovery team was assigned to investigate.

Additional Notes: I have the scp's sort of framework done and its ready for more lore which I am open to suggestions for. This is my first attempt at writing an scp and I am not familiar with too many of them so if there is already an article on a similar idea, my apologies.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: SCP Seeking Greenlight

So let's start

SCP-5156 is to be kept in a 1767.84 centimeters wide cell with special NORA security cameras and iron doors due to SCP-5156's exceptional strength.

What. 1767.84 centimeters? Why so specific? If the cell is 1767.85 will it die? This is a common problem with SCPs (heck I've done it a few times before), you don't need to specify the lengths of the cell. You can just say "SCP-XXXX is to be contained in a humanoid cell."

SCP-5156 is a six foot tall humanoid that looks roughly like a king with white eyes.

Huh? Looks roughly? Weird. Also looking like a king could mean anything. It could be an Egyptian king or a British king etc. You can just say "SCP-XXXX is a humanoid creature that wears a crown (or whatever it is wearing). SCP-XXXX's eyes are completely white as well."

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-5156 is able to merge with anything granting it the body and/or powers due to it's virus.

Ok first off, the footnote could have easily been in the paragraph. Think of footnotes like parentheses. Next, what do you mean by merge with anything? Does it do a body snatcher and replicate them? Or is it like the Thing where it kill and replaces the person. Also what's "it's virus"?

SCP-5156 can speak english, spanish, and french. SCP-5156 is very intelligent and is able to learn very quickly.

I believe the words English, Spanish, and French should be uppercase. Also this is kind of bland to be honest. Like cool it's very smart, it's never brought up again. It just feels like a X-man architype.

SCP-5156 can't attack the person they morph into due to being in the body and if the body SCP-5156 is in gets destroyed so does SCP-5156.

How do they know that? Did SCP-5156 tell them? I guess this is the only "downside" it has. Think of humanoid SCPs as something great (seeing into the future) with unsuspecting consequences (you can't look at food because it will look like feces). That's what made SCP-187 a good SCP since it's a monkey's paw effect. I suggest you also look into more modern humanoid SCPs since SCP-187 is kind of old (but still not terrible).

SCP-5156 was first discovered on 11/██/███ in a factory at ██████ and was found by J████ B████ during a security search at the █████ factory. SCP-5156 was trying to attack J████ B████ due to unknows reasons. SCP-5156 was in a 6 foot box when found for unknown reasons.

Uh, I feel like it was redacted a little too much. I want to at least know the mysterious JB's first name. Also, the factory could've been named to give the SCP more life and interest. Since you would want to know more about the factory. Also did the month have to be blocked out in the date? It seems really silly.

██████: Hello SCP-5156 today you are here so we can find out why you were in a box got it?

Commas can sometimes be annoying but in conversations it can act as a break in a sentence. If I read this sentence out loud then it would be a mouthful. The way I'd put it is "Hello SCP-5156, we have some questions we want to ask."

well I fell out of her body and into the box everybody said I was too dangerous and just kept me in there with the lid closed.

First, well should be capitalized since it was the first word in a sentence. Second, how strong is that box? Earlier you said they had to get iron doors (I think the SCP sites do have iron doors on all SCP cells though) and this smart guy gets trapped in a box? This is also after everyone said he was too dangerous.

After the interview SCP-5156 was taken back to it's cell and the research team started to see if they could get more information about █████████ ██████████ no progress has been achieved.

It's means it is. Its is for referring to objects that posses something. For example, its got a minifridge.

Subject: D-34734
Time: June 27th 4:43 PM EST

The Subject and Time have to be bolded.

Result: SCP-5156 went into D-34734's body as planned and started causing chaos. While the chaos happened a guard removed SCP-5156 from D-34734's body

What kind of chaos? Just saying causing chaos makes the reader less interested in the story.

Analysis: SCP-5156 can cause chaos inside a body but it it very easy to stop.

First you said it was dangerous, and now it's just easy to stop? This is a bit confusing. I suggest going to the forums for help on making your SCP.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn
